{{Short description|Polish mathematician}}
'''Andrzej Pliś''' (March 17, 1929<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7z9FAAAAIAAJ&q=plis&pg=PA124|title = The Review of the Polish Academy of Sciences|page=124|year = 1977|publisher = Assolineum}}</ref> – November 28, 1991<ref name="Łojasiewicz1993">{{cite journal|last1=Łojasiewicz|first1=S.|title=Andrzej Plis (17.3.1929 - 28.11.1991)|journal=Annales Polonici Mathematici|volume=58|issue=2|year=1993|pages=107–109|issn=0066-2216|doi=10.4064/ap-58-2-107-109|doi-access=free}}</ref>) was a Polish mathematician, specializing in differential equations and optimal control theory.

==Education and career==
Pliś received his undergraduate degree from the [[Jagiellonian University]], where he studied from 1947 to 1951.<ref name=obit>{{cite journal|last1=Lojasiewicz|first1=S.|title=In Memoriam: Andrzej Pliś (1929 - 1991)|journal=Journal of Differential Equations|volume=103|issue=1|year=1993|pages=1–2|issn=0022-0396|doi=10.1006/jdeq.1993.1039|bibcode=1993JDE...103....1L|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82447758.pdf|doi-access=free}}</ref> He received his PhD from the Mathematical Institute of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]], where his thesis advisor was [[Tadeusz Ważewski]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=60563}}</ref> Pliś did research and taught at both the Jagiellonian University and the Mathematical Institute of the Polish Academy of Sciences. He was promoted in 1961 to associate professor and in 1966 to full professor. In 1961 he was elected a member of the Polish Academy of Sciences.<ref name=obit/> In 1962 he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Stockholm.<ref>{{cite book|author=Pliś, A.|chapter=Unique continuation theorems for solutions of partial differential equations|title=Proc. Internat. Congr. Mathematicians (Stockholm, 1962)|volume=1|pages=397–402|year=1962}}</ref>

Pliś published about 60 research papers.<ref name=obit/> Perhaps his two most famous papers are ''The problem of uniqueness for the solution of a system of partial differential equations'' (1954) and ''A smooth linear elliptic differential equation without any solution in a sphere'' (1961).<ref name="Morrey Jr.1962">{{cite journal|last1=Morrey Jr.|first1=Charles B.|author-link=Charles B. Morrey Jr.|title=Some recent developments in the theory of partial differential equations|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|volume=68|issue=4|year=1962|pages=279–298|issn=0002-9904|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1962-10765-4|doi-access=free}} (See p. 283; In Morrey's article [[Ennio De Giorgi|De Georgi]] is erroneously referred to as "Di Georgi".)</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dJSNDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA32|isbn = 9783030053031|title = A Pure Soul: Ennio De Giorgi, A Mathematical Genius|date = 18 March 2019|page=32|publisher = Springer}}</ref> His paper ''Characteristics of nonlinear partial differential equations'' (1954) gave an elegant solution to an unsolved problem which [[Alfréd Haar]] worked on in 1929.<ref name=obit/> Another noteworthy paper by Pliś is ''On a topological method for studying the behaviour of the integrals of ordinary differential equations'' (1954).<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C38qE32fqtQC&q=plis|isbn = 9780080532820|title = Handbook of Differential Equations: Ordinary Differential Equations|pages=608 & 683|date = 9 September 2004|publisher = Elsevier}}</ref>
